title: GOD KNEW WHAT PHARAOH WOULD THINK

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Pharaoh will think, 'The Israelites are wandering around the land in confusion,
hemmed in by the desert.' And I will harden Pharaoh's heart, and he will pursue
them. But I will gain glory for myself through Pharaoh and all his army, and the
Egyptians will know that I am the LORD.' So the Israelites did this."
- Ex 14:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God tells Moses in advance exactly what Pharaoh will conclude. He knows the
thoughts of a man who does not know Him at all.

Pharaoh will look at Israel's position and read it as confusion. He will see
weakness and opportunity. He will be completely wrong, and he will act on it.
The very thing that looked like Israel's vulnerability was the bait in God's
trap.

Notice God's stated purpose: "I will gain glory for myself... and the Egyptians
will know that I am the LORD." God is not merely rescuing Israel. He is making
Himself known, even to Egypt.

Scripture again says God will harden Pharaoh's heart, having also said
repeatedly that Pharaoh hardened his own. Believers have long differed over
precisely how these fit together, and this devotional will not settle it. What
Exodus insists on is both: Pharaoh is genuinely responsible for his choices, and
God is genuinely sovereign over the outcome.

The comfort for us is this. What your opponents conclude about you, and how they
act on it, is not outside God's knowledge or control. He is never surprised by
the next move.

And notice the last line: "So the Israelites did this." They obeyed into the
trap.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you afraid of what someone might decide or do about you?
2. Can you obey God even when His instruction seems to expose you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, nothing surprises You and no one outmanoeuvres You. Help me to obey even
when obedience looks like exposure. Amen.
